title: Regional geofence priority lanes and staged-model fallback protocol
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a region-aware 'geofence priority lanes' mechanism that reserves soft capacity for tenants with regional affinity and enforces a staged, quality-first fallback to hosted variants when dedicated lanes saturate or experience degraded SLOs. This ticket covers the routing policy, config surface, observer metrics, and a phased rollout plan.

Background: We've seen several incidents where tenant-affinity routing pushed traffic to a single regional pool and caused either tenant preemption or wide spillover to hosted models with poor quality regressions. Existing work (capacity arbitration and affinity decay) focuses on eviction and coarse demotion; this task introduces explicit soft-reservation lanes with geofence constraints and a multi-step fallback that preserves ranked model variants and region locality where possible.

Requirements:
- New policy type: geofence-priority-lane with parameters: region_set, weight_reservation (pct of lane), expiry_ms, prefetch_window_ms, demotion_thresholds (latency/error/token-rate).
- Soft reservations: Allow tenants to consume up to reservation until a health signal triggers staged demotion rather than immediate spillover.
- Staged fallback chain: primary-dedicated -> geo-compatible-dedicated-variant -> regional-hosted-variant -> global-hosted-variant. Each step must include quality guardrails (similarity score or response-length heuristics) and an automatic rollback window.
- Telemetry: per-tenant and per-route metrics showing reservation usage, demotion events, fallback latency delta, output-quality deltas (from eval-set baseline), and cost delta. Add histograms for time-in-lane before demotion.
- Config surface: Console flags and routing rules via YAML: geofence policy, per-tenant overrides, emergency-evict boolean.
- Safety & degradations: Circuit-breaker that prevents >X% of a region's reservations being surrendered in Y seconds. Blacklist list for known-poor hosted variants per tenant.
- Acceptance criteria: end-to-end test with synthetic traffic, metrics consumer dashboard, a canary rollout to 5 tenants, and a disaster rollback doc.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Soft reservations vs hard guarantees: we chose soft reservations to avoid underutilization and to enable graceful economic sharing. Hard guarantees lead to lower utilization and complicated reclaim logic.
- Prefetch window: adding prefetch (warm KV cache) reduces cold-start latency when a demotion is likely, but increases wasted compute when predictions are wrong. Default prefetch_window_ms is 500ms with tenant opt-out.
- Fallback quality gating: using a lightweight similarity scoring (embed-based pairwise cosine on short samples) is a balance between cost and signal fidelity. We will run an offline eval to set thresholds per model family.
- Telemetry costs: high-cardinality per-tenant metrics are expensive; we'll roll out tenant-level telemetry for the initial canary cohort only and aggregate for others.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (dev): routing policy implementation in the orchestrator (store policy in config store). Implement decision path + basic telemetry hooks (2w).
- Phase 2 (canary): integrate with runtime prefetch and KV warming; deploy to staging and 5 canary tenants with Console controls and dashboards (1w).
- Phase 3 (observability + guardrails): add output-quality scoring, demotion thresholds, eviction circuit-breaker and runbook (1w).
- Phase 4 (rollout): gradual rollout to enterprise tier with monitoring alerts and rollback scripts (2w).

Runbook + docs: Add a 'Geofence priority lanes' section to Console docs and internal runbook. Include playbook: how to force-evict, how to blacklist a hosted variant, and how to change reservation pct.

Links: design doc, runbook, and test harness PRs are listed below in `links`.

Notes: This ticket intentionally avoids changing the global scheduler placement algorithm — we add the geofence lane as a policy overlay that the scheduler respects, to minimize blast radius and simplify testing.
comments: 2025-02-18 Priya Patel: Created ticket after post-incident review (see incident-2025-02-10). Aim: reduce poor-quality spillovers while keeping utilization high.

2025-02-20 Ethan Moore: Initial design spike completed. POC of policy eval in local orchestrator runner. Found that prefetching adds ~12% extra token-cost for false-positive demotions; will add opt-out flag.

2025-02-24 SRE Review (Miguel Santos): Reviewed circuit-breaker thresholds. Suggested adding 'region-wide blackhole' detection to avoid cascading demotions during regional outage. Added as action item.

2025-02-26 Design feedback (Aisha Khan): UX for Console should surface per-tenant reservation usage and a single-click 'force-evict' with confirmation. Also asked for a temporal visualization of demotion events.
2025-02-28 Ethan Moore: Implemented policy storage schema and basic decision path. Pushed draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1123. Unit tests added for chain ordering and TTL expiry.

2025-03-01 QA (Jordan Lee): Ran synthetic workload tests; observed demotion hysteresis too aggressive (too fast demotion) — increased demotion_threshold window from 3s->7s. Will validate with canary tenants next week.
2025-03-02 Priya Patel: Updated acceptance criteria and added canary list. Next: schedule canary deployment and prepare dashboard panels for SLO owners.
